events.text:
Two levels up, the only real caller is the REST checkout endpoint:

- Level 1 (direct callers of `priceShoppingCart`): `CartEndpoint.add` :50, `delete` :101, `set` :77, and `ShoppingCartService.checkOutShoppingCart` :43.
- Level 2 (callers of those): `CartEndpoint.checkout` :43 → calls `checkOutShoppingCart`.

`add`, `delete`, and `set` are `@POST`/`@DELETE` REST handlers with no internal callers, so the chain terminates there. (`checkout` itself is a JAX-RS boundary entry point, invoked by the container, not code.)

One caveat: rgctl also reported `Transformers.shoppingCartToJson` (:48) as a caller of `add`, but that's a name-collision false positive from `java.util.List.add`, not a call to `CartEndpoint.add`.

So the call chain is: `CartEndpoint.checkout` → `ShoppingCartService.checkOutShoppingCart` → `priceShoppingCart`.

Evidence: rgctl `callers priceShoppingCart` plus callers for each level-one node; confirmed at CartEndpoint.java:43-44.

For `CartEndpoint` (`com.redhat.coolstore.rest.CartEndpoint`):

**`exposesroute` — 10 edges** (method → route; rgctl reports the annotation line):
- `getCart` :33 → `GET /cart`, `GET /cart/{cartId}`
- `checkout` :40 → `POST /cart`, `GET /cart/checkout/{cartId}`
- `add` :47 → `POST /cart`, `GET /cart/{cartId}/{itemId}/{quantity}`
- `set` :74 → `POST /cart`, `GET /cart/{cartId}/{tmpId}`
- `delete` :98 → `DELETE /cart`, `GET /cart/{cartId}/{itemId}/{quantity}`

**`injects` — 1 edge:**
- `CartEndpoint` :24 → `ShoppingCartService` (`com.redhat.coolstore.service.ShoppingCartService`, ShoppingCartService.java:16)

Note: the class-level `relations -e exposesroute CartEndpoint` returned zero because route edges attach to the methods, not the class; I had to do a seedless scan and filter to the `CartEndpoint` source. Also, `--file` did not actually filter — it dumped all 16 route edges repo-wide (including `OrderEndpoint`/`ProductEndpoint`), so I filtered by qualified name. rbctl evidence: `/tmp/er.json`, `relations -e injects`.

The `GET /cart` / `POST /cart` class-relative edges encode the `@Path("/cart")` prefix paired with each verb, which is why every method yields two edges.

The GET /cart / POST /cart class-relative edges encode the @Path("/cart") prefix paired with each verb, which is why every method yields two edges.

Usage: rgctl [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>

Commands:
Lifecycle:
  discover      Index and analyze a codebase
  status        Session graph status (snapshot presence, digest, node/edge counts, source staleness; no rediscover)
  update        Incremental structural graph update for changed files (not a full discover / analysis rebuild)
  watch         Watch the repo and apply incremental graph updates on save (`notify`, default 25ms debounce)
  merge         Merge multiple discovered repos, resolving parked cross-repo relations
  serve         Serve the universe dashboard and GQL query API over HTTP
  diff          Diff two columnar graph snapshots (cold diff profiling / compare path)

Query:
  find          Find symbols by name/type over the mmap graph index (no GQL)
  callers       Incoming CALLS neighbors for a symbol
  callees       Outgoing CALLS neighbors for a symbol
  relations     Typed edge traversal; omit SYMBOL for seedless set-wide scan
  inventory     Aggregate symbol/edge counts (includes zero-count schema kinds for type/edge)
  gql           Experimental graph query language — prefer `find` / `callers` / `relations` / `inventory` for common queries

Analysis:
  blast-radius  Macro impact / blast radius for a symbol
  slice         Line-level program slice or taint trace (builds & caches single-function CFG/PDG lazily on demand)
  taint         Sink-first taint (`--sink` + `--source external`); requires `discover --with-cfg`
  inspect       Inspect raw CFG / PDG / dominance for a function symbol
  metrics       Network & churn analytics (PageRank, betweenness, communities, git churn)
  semantic      Opt-in semantic search over function symbols (separate index artifact)
  communities   List or refresh named communities (analysis overlay)
  clones        Clone detection: exact Type-1 (`code_hash`), Type-2 Bloom LSH, or Type-3/4 SESE+1-WL fragments

  dead-code     Dead-code detection via graph reachability analysis

Security:
  vuln          OSV vulnerability triage / analyze

  help          Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Other:
  writeback     Lossless reconstruct / verify / patch Tier-1 sources from `.rgctl/` sidecars
